subject: biology
title: Evolution & Biodiversity Adventure 1: Natural selection and evidence
welcome_lead: Today you'll follow Darwin from finch to fossil — and the evidence for evolution.
meta_desc: IBDP Biology — natural selection, Darwin 1859, evidence (fossils, biogeography, homology), antibiotic resistance.
final_note: You learned natural selection acts on heritable variation, fossils, biogeography and homology support common descent, and antibiotic resistance is evolution in action.

walkthroughs.body_html:
From On the Origin of Species (1859):

1. Populations show variation.
2. More offspring born than survive.
3. Some variants are better suited (fitter).
4. Survivors pass on traits.
5. Over generations, the population evolves.

Wallace independently reached the same conclusion in 1858 — joint paper to the Linnean Society.

- Fossil record — transitional forms (Archaeopteryx, Tiktaalik).
- Biogeography — Galápagos finches, marsupials in Australia.
- Homology — tetrapod pentadactyl limb (human, bat, whale, dog).
- Molecular — DNA + protein sequence similarity tracks phylogeny.

Antibiotic resistance: a few bacteria carry resistance alleles (e.g. β-lactamase). Antibiotic kills susceptible; resistant survive and reproduce.

MRSA cases tripled 1995-2005 in UK hospitals before infection control improvements.

Peppered moth Biston betularia — dark form rose to 95% in industrial Manchester (1850s), reversed after Clean Air Act.
